params.baseInstructions: Complete the supplied mathematical task using only its explicit inputs and tools. Submit the requested JSON artifact through structured submit_draft (preferred) or the compatible submit_artifact wrapper. Tool feedback is real task feedback; do not invent a successful check. This is a Yui workflow stage. Read the relevant declared Yui rules, preserve the supplied proof route and exact allowed assumptions, and distinguish mathematical review from structural checks.

dynamicTools.name: search_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: 在固定 mathlib 的 Lean 源码中搜索正则表达式，返回至多 100 行。

dynamicTools.name: read_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: 读取固定 mathlib 中一个 Mathlib/...lean 文件的指定行。

dynamicTools.name: read_task_input
dynamicTools.description: Read an explicitly frozen task document by ID; no other local files are accessible.

dynamicTools.name: read_yui
dynamicTools.description: Read declared Yui rules/templates; no tests, historical runs or personal files.

dynamicTools.name: check_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Check a JSON artifact against the explicit stage contract; this is not automatic mathematical certification.

dynamicTools.name: submit_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Submit a JSON artifact after its stage checks.

dynamicTools.name: report_obstacle
dynamicTools.description: Report exact status, location, explanation, basis, partial_progress. SUBSTANTIVE_GAP or SUSPECTED_GAP stops for an actual unsupported mathematical implication; give its premises, conclusion and mathematical grounds. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or INPUT_CONFLICT stops for a real source-access/original-input obstacle. Ordinary unfinished drafting, source registration or format work must use TASK_INCOMPLETE: this records progress without ending the stage; continue the actual work. Difficulty or artifact incompletion alone is not a mathematical gap.

dynamicTools.name: check_draft
dynamicTools.description: Preferred structured-object form of check_artifact: provide artifact as an actual JSON object, not an escaped JSON string. Same complete validation and acceptance scope.

dynamicTools.name: submit_draft
dynamicTools.description: Preferred structured-object form of submit_artifact: provide artifact as an actual JSON object, not an escaped JSON string. Same complete validation and acceptance scope.

dynamicTools.name: probe_library
dynamicTools.description: Query a proved Mathlib theorem and its exact signature/axioms in the offline sandbox. Returns located evidence for an M source; the mathematical statement and applicability still require review.

dynamicTools.name: read_draft
dynamicTools.description: Read a JSON pointer in your own same-stage candidate after an actual structural check. No other file/stage is accessible; choose a narrow pointer for large objects.

input.text:
Repair only the actual outstanding local proof/source closure of the supplied geometry candidate. Read the actual global and packet-only reviews. A review finding is a mathematical claim to check, not an authority that changes the original problem. In particular independently verify the enlarged-index slicing-cover implication from E×I⊆union V_i and B_i⊆J_i; do not accept or reject a review complaint by its label. The selected-model-measure-bridge contains the original explicit elementary argument. Preserve the upper covering/slicing/projection route and original H/target. The packet reviewer identified an actual missing measure monotonicity/restricted-measure comparison: register and apply the full corresponding general pinned theorem(s) or genuinely prove the implication locally. Also explicitly discharge interval restricted mass=1, measurability, ambient finiteness and each genuine source/application condition. Expand the existing upper small-cost-cover inference from the exact supremum/infimum formula, its zero-diameter replacement, countable product cover and cost bound; do not merely rename these steps. Expand the epsilon-to-infimum step explicitly, including empty/zero-cost members and positive-exponent conventions. None of these requires changing the target or searching a new core proof. Reprobe every retained M in this fresh stage, preserving its actual complete source restatement. Update direct inputs, uses, citation/application and object accounting together. Use the new hash-bound own-stage checkpoint and read_draft/base_candidate to preserve your accumulated work after any context reset. A structural pass is only a candidate for independent Audit A; submit the completed candidate without claiming a mathematical audit. Routine unfinished work should continue, not become a false substantive-gap report.
Canonical submission has exactly {"spec": <NL0 v2 specification>, "graph": <NL0 v2 graph>}. For a local revision, you may instead submit {"base_input":"<frozen task document ID>", "patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"/graph/...","value":...}]}. That declared task document must itself contain {spec,graph}; supported JSON edit operations are add/remove/replace/test with absolute JSON pointers inside spec or graph. Edits always start from that immutable base, not the last rejected edit. Array append uses /-. The expanded result undergoes every ordinary metadata/source/structure gate and later Audit A. This saves retyping unchanged content; it does not change mathematical authority. After check_artifact gives candidate_number N, you may also submit {"base_candidate":N,"patches":[...]} to edit that exact own same-stage draft. Use read_draft(candidate=N,pointer="/graph/inferences/0") to inspect it. Submit {"accept_candidate":N} to resubmit that exact own draft without retyping it. Once a same-stage candidate exists, restarting edits from a frozen base_input requires explicit reset_base:true, because it discards accumulated edits. Candidates from another stage and undeclared files are unavailable. The controller binds spec.inputs to all frozen task documents, pins to the verified runtime, and graph.spec_sha256 to the resulting spec. Supply these fields as placeholders if needed. All mathematical fields remain your responsibility. probe_library returns checked M-source evidence inside this stage case directory. The controller binds M signature, source hashes, declaration kind, commit and evidence from the actual successful probe matching its ID, declaration and dotted module. These metadata fields may be omitted; never transcribe or fabricate them. It does not change source.statement, hypotheses, binders or proof text; all still need complete mathematical content. Redundant aliases may also be omitted: H graph statement copies its own spec.hypotheses statement, P statement copies spec.conclusion, and E/M source.statement copies its primary proposition.statement. Existing conflicting texts are rejected, never silently rewritten. Actual source signatures/source_statement remain separate fidelity obligations. A successful check_artifact is structural validation, not Audit A acceptance.
Frozen structural contract: spec.format_version=2; graph.format_version=2; spec.case_id=graph.case_id="geometry-product-dimension". The controller-bound pins are {"lean_version": "4.32.2", "mathlib_commit": "905b95818eb32af7874a58b427f50c1711a5e96c", "mathlib_root": "/Users/syyui/formalization-tools/lean-mathlib-v4.32.2/mathlib"}. These are provided configuration facts, not guessed mathematical premises. Spec.inputs, spec.pins and graph.spec_sha256 are rebound deterministically, so their placeholder values are not an input conflict. All other required schema fields must be supplied normally.
Exact permitted machine rule names for spec.logic.rules and inference.rules: ["case_elimination", "contradiction_classical", "direct", "exists_elimination", "forall_introduction", "implication_introduction", "modus_ponens", "natural_induction", "negation_introduction"]. Use these identifiers; put mathematical derivations in argument text, not invented rule enum values. Parameters are a list of {symbol,type}; logic is an object {classical,rules,calculations,primitives}. Inferences use R001-style IDs; argument paragraphs use S001-style IDs; propositions use H001/E001/M001/N001 or P. An unknown field/rule is a format repair, not a mathematical gap. Read references/nl0-format.md for every remaining field.
Yui entry: read_yui(path="SKILL.md", start=1, end=200). Available frozen rule paths (relative to rigorous-proof): SKILL.md, references/audit-a.md, references/external-theorems.md, references/isolation.md, references/lean-handoff.md, references/logical-rules.md, references/measurement.md, references/nl0-authoring.md, references/nl0-format.md, references/nl0-stage.md, references/self-containment.md, templates/audit-a.md, templates/authoring.md, templates/submission-example.md, translation/references/architecture.md, translation/references/audit-b.md, translation/references/design-notes.md, translation/references/experiments.md, translation/references/integrated-workflow.md, translation/references/obstacle-routing.md, translation/references/shared-lemmas.md, translation/references/source-refactoring.md, translation/references/stage.md, translation/references/translation-rules.md, translation/references/workflow.md, translation/templates/audit-b.md, translation/templates/source-refactoring.md. Every read supports at most 250 lines. Start with the entry and follow its relevant links; do not guess filenames.
Frozen task document IDs: actual-review-findings.json, frozen-target.md, prior-candidate.json, problem.md, prompt.txt, selected-model-measure-bridge.json, source-context.md. Use read_task_input to read them.
Prefer check_draft/submit_draft with an actual artifact JSON object. The older check_artifact/submit_artifact wrappers require artifact_json to be a double-encoded valid JSON string; do not supply Python dictionaries or single-quoted keys. Both forms run identical checks.
